question: Can per-decision DFA eviction bound TypeScript memory under Node's default heap without the latency cost of whole-cache clearing?
control: Official-grammar TypeScript baseline with persistent generated DFA caches under an 8 GB old-space limit.
candidate: Opt-in per-decision bounds: enforce every 10 files; cap hot decisions at 90,000 states; cap cold decisions at 2,000 states; treat decisions 2993, 2251, 2990, and 2595 as hot.

commands.performance: for i in 1 2 3; do env -u NODE_OPTIONS LAB_DFA_SELECTIVE_EVERY=10 LAB_DFA_HOT_DECISIONS=2993,2251,2990,2595 LAB_DFA_HOT_MAX_STATES=90000 LAB_DFA_COLD_MAX_STATES=2000 pnpm dfa:eviction -- --experiment 018-selective-dfa-eviction-r$i; done
commands.conformance: env -u NODE_OPTIONS LAB_DFA_SELECTIVE_EVERY=10 LAB_DFA_HOT_DECISIONS=2993,2251,2990,2595 LAB_DFA_HOT_MAX_STATES=90000 LAB_DFA_COLD_MAX_STATES=2000 pnpm dfa:eviction -- --experiment 018-selective-dfa-eviction --tree-hash --observations .work/018-candidate-observations.json --compare .work/018-control-observations.json

selection: Complete frozen 1,244-file opaque production corpus; three fresh-process performance passes, a paired host-load control session, and a complete tree/diagnostic comparison.
acceptance: Complete every pass under Node's default heap.
Preserve parse trees, tokens, diagnostics, acceptance, and fallback semantics.
Reduce peak RSS without the 22–38% whole-cache latency regression.
Use state bounds that do not depend on corpus identities or fixed production file order.
Reject and document candidates that fail the memory or latency gate.
